source.author: hor
source.text: Si curatus inaequali tonsore capillos occurri, rides; si forte subucula pexae trita subest tunicae, vel si toga dissidet impar, rides: quid, mea cum pugnat sententia secum, quod petiit spernit, repetit quod nuper omisit, aestuat et vitae disconvenit ordine toto, diruit, aedificat, mutat quadrata rotundis?
source.text_original: Si curatus inaequali tonsore capillos / occurri, rides; si forte subucula pexae  / trita subest tunicae, vel si toga dissidet impar, / rides: quid, mea cum pugnat sententia secum, / quod petiit spernit, repetit quod nuper omisit, / aestuat et vitae disconvenit ordine toto, / diruit, aedificat, mutat quadrata rotundis?
source.text_english: If, when I have had my hair trimmed by an uneven barber, I meet you, you laugh; if by chance a worn undershirt is under my brushed tunic, or if my toga sits awry, you laugh. But why, when my judgment is at war with itself, when it spurns what it sought, takes up again what it recently let go, boils and is out of step with the whole order of life—pulling down, building up, changing squares for circles?

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text_english: He tears down, builds up, changes squares into circles.
